intro.speaker: Maya
intro.text_en: You made it! People have watched this sky for ages. Tonight, you join that long chain with a record of your own.
intro.text_zh: 你终于来啦！我是玛雅，也是天文社的学姐~从今天开始，你也算正式加入我们天文社这个大家庭啦！人们仰望这片天空已经很久很久了，不过今晚嘛，就该轮到我们的小观测员，亲手写下自己的第一笔啦~

intro.speaker: Maya
intro.text_en: Hands off the telescope for one minute. Start with the Moon and your own eyes—shape, dark patches, and all the detail that refuses to show itself.
intro.text_zh: 小观测员~望远镜待会儿再碰！先用眼睛看看月球的轮廓和那些暗斑，也记住哪些地方怎么盯都看不清，等会儿你就知道望远镜到底做什么用啦~

intro.speaker: Maya
intro.text_en: Our routine is simple: take the question from the board, choose parts at the Parts Cabinet, build at the Assembly Table, observe, then keep the evidence in the Club Logbook.
intro.text_zh: 流程其实很简单啦~先去任务板领题，再到零件柜挑部件，组装台把望远镜装好，接着就能去观测啦！看完记得回来把结果写进观测日志哦~

intro.speaker: Maya
intro.text_en: The round platform in the middle is our Observation Pad. The green terminal can wait; tonight, your eyes get the first shift.
intro.text_zh: 看到中间那个望远镜了吗？那就是我们的观测台啦~右下角那台绿屏终端先别管它！~

intro.speaker: You
intro.text_en: So the first record is not supposed to be perfect?
intro.text_zh: 所以第一份记录本来就不需要完美？

intro.speaker: Maya
intro.text_en: Exactly. Record the shape and dark patches first; on our second Moon visit, a refractor will show us the crater rims for comparison.
intro.text_zh: 对对，就先把现在肉眼能看到的样子记下来~

intro.speaker: Maya
intro.text_en: We'll do the first ten lessons here at the club. Use WASD to walk to the Observation Pad and press E to enter, then use A/D and W/S to center the Moon. I'll stay in the hall and wait for your observing log.
intro.text_zh: 前十节基础课都在社团里完成。你先用 WASD 走到观测台，按 E 进入，再用 A/D 和 W/S 把月球移到中央。我会留在大厅等你的观测日志。

intro.speaker: Maya
intro.text_en: Keep tonight's naked-eye record. Next time we'll use a refractor to see the crater rims and compare the two~
intro.text_zh: 今晚这份肉眼记录要留好哦。下次换折射镜看环形山边缘，两份日志正好对照~

level_2_after.speaker: Maya
level_2_after.text_en: Polaris showed you north, but not much structure. That's your eyes reaching their limit—not you doing anything wrong.
level_2_after.text_zh: 北极星认出来啦？它可是夜空里很好用的“方向标”~不过光靠肉眼，还是只能看到一个小亮点，细节该轮到望远镜上场了！

level_2_after.speaker: Maya
level_2_after.text_en: So let's build a bigger eye. Check the Mission Board, collect the parts, and meet me at the Assembly Table.
level_2_after.text_zh: 先去任务板看看今晚要观测什么吧~再到零件柜把该拿的部件都找齐，准备好了就来组装台找我，我在这边等你！

level_3_before_assembly.speaker: Maya
level_3_before_assembly.text_en: Your first Moon record caught the outline and maria, but the crater rims stayed hidden. Good—that gives our refractor a fair challenge.
level_3_before_assembly.text_zh: 还记得第一份月球记录吧？轮廓和月海都有了，可那些小环形山还是糊糊的~这次就换折射望远镜上场，把之前没看清的细节一点点补回来！

level_3_before_assembly.speaker: Maya
level_3_before_assembly.text_en: Galileo didn't invent the telescope, but in the early 1600s he improved one and aimed it upward. Suddenly the Moon wasn't a smooth disc; it had real, uneven ground.
level_3_before_assembly.text_zh: 17 世纪初，伽利略把望远镜改得更好用，还真的把它指向了天空~望远镜不是他发明的，不过从那以后，月球在人们眼里就不只是一个亮圆盘啦，山脉、凹坑和那些起伏的地形，第一次变得清清楚楚了

level_3_before_assembly.speaker: Maya
level_3_before_assembly.text_en: Build the refractor in optical order, then revisit the same Moon. Compare those crater rims with your first entry—that difference is the whole point.
level_3_before_assembly.text_zh: 接下来该让望远镜上场啦~按着光路顺序把折射镜一点点装好，再去看看月球！记得拿第一份日志出来对照一下，看看这次是不是连环形山的边缘都冒出了好多新细节呀~

level_6_before.speaker: Maya
level_6_before.text_en: That main-scope view is a keyhole. Experienced observers lose targets too, so don't blame your eyes—the patch of sky really is that tiny.
level_6_before.text_zh: 主镜的视野本来就窄得可怜，找不到目标真的太正常啦，连老手都会一不留神把它弄丢~所以先别怀疑自己的眼神，视野确实就这么大呀！

level_6_before.speaker: Maya
level_6_before.text_en: That's why we add a little wide-field finder. It gives no planet detail; it just gets the target through that keyhole.
level_6_before.text_zh: 所以主镜旁边还会带一支宽视场的寻星镜呀~它先帮我们把目标找进来，再交给主镜慢慢看！

level_6_before.speaker: Maya
level_6_before.text_en: First, use Sirius to align the finder with the main telescope. When you observe, follow this order: get your bearings with your eyes, catch the target in the finder, then switch to the main telescope for the details.
level_6_before.text_zh: 先用天狼星把寻星镜和主镜对齐。观测时按这个顺序来：先用肉眼认方向，再用寻星镜捕捉目标，最后切到主镜看细节。

level_6_before.speaker: Maya
level_6_before.text_en: But line it up with the main scope first. Otherwise it will point to the wrong patch of sky with impressive confidence.
level_6_before.text_zh: 先拿天狼星把寻星镜和主镜对齐好~以后就记住这个顺序呀：肉眼先找出方向，寻星镜负责把目标对准到差不多，等它在视野里了，再交给主镜看细节！

level_10_after.speaker: Maya
level_10_after.text_en: You can build, aim, and focus the refractor now. Nice. From here on, the telescope isn't the only thing with opinions.
level_10_after.text_zh: 折射镜这边你已经很熟练啦~接下来可不是望远镜了……这片天空。

level_10_after.speaker: Maya
level_10_after.text_en: Dark adaptation, clouds, shaky air, Earth's rotation—the gear stays familiar, but the sky won't. Time to learn when to adjust and when to wait.
level_10_after.text_zh: 后面的夜晚可就没这么省心啦~暗适应、云层、大气抖动，还有地球自己在转，都会来添点麻烦。望远镜还是那一台，但你得慢慢等一等。

level_18_after.speaker: Maya
level_18_after.text_en: You've learned to read the sky instead of taking clouds, drift, and bad seeing as random punishment. Fix what you can; when fiddling would only make it worse, wait it out.
level_18_after.text_zh: 你已经会读天空了：能修的就修，越动越糟时就耐心等。

level_18_after.speaker: Maya
level_18_after.text_en: No more practicing one control at a time. The Mission Board gives you the goal; how to set up the observatory and when to wait on the weather are your calls.
level_18_after.text_zh: 接下来不拆成单项练习啦。任务板给目标，设备怎么配、天气怎么等，都由你安排。

level_18_before.speaker: Maya
level_18_before.text_en: Bright planets answer at a glance. Deep-sky objects can begin as almost nothing, so don't be too quick to doubt your eyes.
level_18_before.text_zh: 亮行星一眼就有回应，深空天体却常淡得像什么都没有。别急着怀疑自己的眼睛。

level_18_before.speaker: Maya
level_18_before.text_en: The club's older notebooks say it again and again: more aperture, dark-adapted eyes, darker skies, and patience. Faint structure reveals itself bit by bit.
level_18_before.text_zh: 社团旧日志反复写着：大口径、暗适应、暗天空，再加耐心，淡结构才会一点点显出来。

level_18_before.speaker: Maya
level_18_before.text_en: Hold the Orion Nebula steady and give it a quiet moment. That soft glow traveled about 1,300 years to reach us; it doesn't need to shout to count as evidence.
level_18_before.text_zh: 稳住猎户座星云，安静多看一会儿。那团微光走了约1300年才抵达我们，柔柔亮着就已经是证据。

level_24_after.speaker: Maya
level_24_after.text_en: You chose the gear, set it up, and made the observation all on your own. You've proved you can run the full refractor workflow.
level_24_after.text_zh: 选设备、架设、观测，全是你独立完成。折射镜这套流程，你已经稳稳走通了。

level_24_after.speaker: Maya
level_24_after.text_en: One look at Vega's color fringe isn't enough to call it. Tomorrow we'll return to the same star, change nothing, and refocus carefully to see whether it stays. The next optical clue is in the club storeroom~
level_24_after.text_zh: 织女星那圈彩边，光看一回还不能下结论。明晚再看同一颗星，什么都别乱换，只认真调焦核对一次。下一份光学线索在储藏室~

level_25_before.speaker: Maya
level_25_before.text_en: Vega is bright, distant and nearly point-like. That makes it an unforgiving test: a perfect star image should be compact and colorless.
level_25_before.text_zh: 织女星又亮又远，在镜里几乎就是一个点，最适合检查彩边。理想的星点应该小而干净。

level_25_before.speaker: Maya
level_25_before.text_en: Focus as carefully as you know how. If the colored fringe remains at best focus, do not blame your hands. We are testing the lens design itself.
level_25_before.text_zh: 先把焦点调到最清楚。要是彩边还在，别怪自己手抖，那是透镜留下来的。

level_25_after.speaker: Maya
level_25_after.text_en: The fringe survived best focus. Different colors were bent by different amounts, so the refractor could not bring them to one point.
level_25_after.text_zh: 彩边在最佳焦点仍然存在。不同颜色被透镜弯折的程度不同，因此折射镜无法让它们落在同一点。

level_25_after.speaker: Maya
level_25_after.text_en: That failure gives us the reason to change telescope families. At the blueprint selector, choose the Newtonian: mirrors reflect all visible colors along the same path.
level_25_after.text_zh: 所以我们换一种思路。去蓝图选择器切到牛顿式，镜面反射不会把不同颜色拆开。

level_26_before_assembly.speaker: Maya
level_26_before_assembly.text_en: You focused Vega correctly and the colored fringe remained. Breathe: that was not your mistake. The refractor reached its own physical limit, and that is how science asks for a new tool.
level_26_before_assembly.text_zh: 织女星已经合焦，彩边却还在。先松口气，这不是你调错了，是折射镜碰到了自己的极限。

level_26_before_assembly.speaker: Maya
level_26_before_assembly.text_en: Isaac Newton built a practical reflecting telescope to avoid the color separation caused by large lenses. A curved primary gathers the light; a small secondary turns it toward a side focuser.
level_26_before_assembly.text_zh: 艾萨克·牛顿制造了实用反射望远镜，以避开大型透镜造成的颜色分离。弯曲主镜负责集光，小副镜把光转向侧置调焦器。

level_26_before_assembly.speaker: Maya
level_26_before_assembly.text_en: Open the Newtonian blueprint. Build the primary, secondary, spider, and side focuser as one path, then collimate their shared axis. Mirrors solve the color problem by giving you a new responsibility.
level_26_before_assembly.text_zh: 打开牛顿式蓝图，装好主镜、副镜、蜘蛛支架和侧置调焦器。装完还要准直，让几块镜面的光轴对齐。

level_35_after.speaker: Maya
level_35_after.text_en: The Newtonian proved the bargain: no lens color fringe, more aperture for the cost, and a new responsibility to collimate the mirrors.
level_35_after.text_zh: 牛顿式没有透镜彩边，同样预算还能做得更大。不过镜面要靠你准直，这是它多出来的功课。

level_35_after.speaker: Maya
level_35_after.text_en: Next we keep that same optical path but simplify the mount. The saved complexity becomes a larger mirror, and tracking moves from machinery into your hands.
level_35_after.text_zh: 下一台还用牛顿光路，但把支架做得更简单，省下的钱换成更大的主镜。代价是追踪得靠手推。

level_36_before_assembly.speaker: Maya
level_36_before_assembly.text_en: The Newtonian worked, but large-aperture astronomy could still feel expensive, mechanical, and far from ordinary people.
level_36_before_assembly.text_zh: 牛顿光路已经成立，但大口径天文观测仍可能显得昂贵、机械结构复杂，离普通人很远。

level_36_before_assembly.speaker: Maya
level_36_before_assembly.text_en: John Dobson popularized big Newtonian tubes on simple rocker boxes and brought them to public sidewalks. Big mirrors could belong to a shared night outside, not only an elite observatory.
level_36_before_assembly.text_zh: 约翰·多布森推广了装在简单摇箱上的大口径牛顿镜，并把它们带到街头公众观测。大主镜可以属于大家共享的户外夜晚，而不只属于少数专业台站。

level_36_before_assembly.speaker: Maya
level_36_before_assembly.text_en: Choose the Dobsonian blueprint. Frame a wide deep-sky field, gather faint light, and supply the tracking yourself with gentle altitude-azimuth nudges. Imagine another club member waiting for their turn.
level_36_before_assembly.text_zh: 选择多布森蓝图。用宽视场容纳深空目标、收集暗弱光线，再用轻柔的经纬式推镜亲手追踪。想象还有一位社员正等着轮到自己看。

level_45_after.speaker: Maya
level_45_after.text_en: The Dobsonian made faint light affordable, and you learned to supply the tracking its mount does not provide.
level_45_after.text_zh: 多布森式让暗弱光线变得触手可及，你也学会了用双手补上支架没有提供的追踪。

level_45_after.speaker: Maya
level_45_after.text_en: But aperture and a wide manual sweep are not ideal for every target. Fine planetary structure asks for a long focal length in a compact, precisely aimed tube.
level_45_after.text_zh: 但大口径和宽广的手动扫掠并不适合所有目标。细小的行星结构需要长焦距、紧凑镜筒和更精确的指向。

level_46_before_assembly.speaker: Maya
level_46_before_assembly.text_en: Aperture and a wide sweep are wonderful for faint fields, but tiny planetary detail asks for a long focal length. A truly long tube is awkward to carry, support, and aim.
level_46_before_assembly.text_zh: 大口径和宽广扫掠很适合暗弱天区，但行星上的小细节需要长焦距。镜筒如果真做得很长，搬运、支撑和瞄准都会很麻烦。

level_46_before_assembly.speaker: Maya
level_46_before_assembly.text_en: A two-mirror design published under Laurent Cassegrain's name in 1672 folded the optical path back through the primary, packing long focal length into a compact body.
level_46_before_assembly.text_zh: 1672 年以洛朗·卡塞格林之名发表的双镜设计，让光路折返并穿过主镜，把长焦距装进紧凑镜身。

level_46_before_assembly.speaker: Maya
level_46_before_assembly.text_en: Build it, then use the finder with discipline. Its narrow main field will punish a rushed hand, but careful pointing earns high-magnification planetary detail.
level_46_before_assembly.text_zh: 把它装起来，找目标时别跳过寻星镜。主镜视野窄，慢一点对准，才能换来高倍率下的行星细节。

level_55_after.speaker: Maya
level_55_after.text_en: You have now changed aperture, focal length, mount and light path on the ground. Each solved one problem and created another.
level_55_after.text_zh: 你已经换过口径、焦距、支架和光路。每种设计都有擅长的目标，也都有要迁就的地方。

level_55_after.speaker: Maya
level_55_after.text_en: The next limits cannot be fixed by another ground-telescope shape: our atmosphere blocks wavelengths and blurs detail. We move to the Space Telescope Console and change both location and wavelength.
level_55_after.text_zh: 再换地面镜筒也绕不过大气：有些波段会被挡住，细节也会被扰动抹掉。下一站去空间望远镜控制台。

level_66_before_assembly.speaker: Maya
level_66_before_assembly.text_en: Our atmosphere is not an enemy; it protects us. But it absorbs important infrared wavelengths, and warm air and warm telescopes glow in infrared too, hiding faint signals.
level_66_before_assembly.text_zh: 大气保护着我们，但也会挡住一部分红外。空气和望远镜只要有温度，还会自己发出红外，把微弱目标盖住。

level_66_before_assembly.speaker: Maya
level_66_before_assembly.text_en: Modern cold infrared observatories operate beyond Earth, including near Sun-Earth L2. Distance, a sunshield, and deep cooling let them protect photons our ground instruments cannot keep clean.
level_66_before_assembly.text_zh: 所以红外望远镜会去太空，像日地 L2 附近那样远离地面。遮阳罩和低温环境能把仪器自己的热辐射压下去。

level_66_before_assembly.speaker: Maya
level_66_before_assembly.text_en: There is no eyepiece now. Assemble the remote observatory, then use the Space Console to deploy it, protect its cold side, lock a guide star, align wavefronts, accumulate photons, process frames, and map filters.
level_66_before_assembly.text_zh: 这次没有目镜。先把远程观测站装好，再到空间控制台一步步展开、热控、导星、对准、曝光和处理。

level_75_after.speaker: Maya
level_75_after.text_en: Infrared proved that changing wavelength can reveal structure invisible from the ground. An astronomical image is already more than what the eye sees.
level_75_after.text_zh: 换到红外以后，尘埃后面的结构也露出来了。天文图像不只记录眼睛能看见的光。

level_75_after.speaker: Maya
level_75_after.text_en: FAST takes the final step: there is no eyepiece picture at all. At the radio console, frequency, timing and signal strength become the observation.
level_75_after.text_zh: FAST 更不一样，它根本不给你目镜画面。你要看的，是频率、周期和信号强度。

level_76_before_assembly.speaker: Maya
level_76_before_assembly.text_en: Infrared taught us that an image can be processed data. Radio astronomy goes further: some sources give us no useful picture at all, only a repeating pattern buried in noise.
level_76_before_assembly.text_zh: 红外图像已经离不开数据处理。到了射电这边，有些天体连照片都没有，只在噪声里留下一遍遍重复的节奏。

level_76_before_assembly.speaker: Maya
level_76_before_assembly.text_en: FAST is a 500-meter radio telescope in Guizhou. Its active reflector reshapes below a suspended feed cabin, directing radio waves into receivers that turn an invisible sky into measurable signals.
level_76_before_assembly.text_zh: FAST 在贵州，口径 500 米。下面的主动反射面会变形，把射电波汇聚到悬吊馈源舱里的接收机。

level_76_before_assembly.speaker: Maya
level_76_before_assembly.text_en: Assemble the signal chain, then position the feed cabin, tune frequency, reject RFI, fold pulses, match dispersion measure, integrate longer, and raise SNR. This time the trace is the evidence.
level_76_before_assembly.text_zh: 先把信号链装好。进入控制台后，稳住馈源舱、找对频段、清掉干扰，再调周期和色散量，按住积分把脉冲从噪声里拉出来。

level_85_after.speaker: Maya
level_85_after.text_en: You began by centering the Moon with your eyes. Now you can extract the period of an invisible dead star from noise. The instruments changed, but the method did not: ask, predict, measure, compare, record.
level_85_after.text_zh: 最开始，你只是用肉眼把月球移到中央。现在，你能从噪声里找出一颗脉冲星的周期了。仪器变了，耐心观察和认真记录没变。

level_85_after.speaker: Maya
level_85_after.text_en: That is the observatory's real lesson. No telescope is the final upgrade; each is an answer to a particular kind of light and a particular scientific question. Your Club Logbook is the proof that you learned to choose.
level_85_after.text_zh: 没有哪台望远镜能包办所有目标。你已经会看目标、看波段，再挑合适的工具。翻翻俱乐部日志吧，这一路都记在里面。

first_tube_subassembly.speaker: Maya
first_tube_subassembly.text_en: The main blueprint shows where the completed tube belongs, but it cannot explain what happens inside it. Open the Tube Blueprint first.
first_tube_subassembly.text_zh: 主蓝图只留了一个完整镜筒槽位。先打开镜筒子装配，把里面的光路装好。

first_tube_subassembly.speaker: Maya
first_tube_subassembly.text_en: Build the mirrors, spider and focuser as one optical path. When that path is complete, save the tube and return it to the main Assembly Table.
first_tube_subassembly.text_zh: 依次装上镜面、蜘蛛支架和调焦器。镜筒保存后会回到主装配台，再把它装进整机。

first_collimation.speaker: Maya
first_collimation.text_en: Assembly decides whether the parts are present. Collimation decides whether their optical axes agree. A reflector can be complete and still form a distorted star.
first_collimation.text_zh: 零件装齐了，不代表光路就正。反射镜如果没准直，星点还是会歪、会散。

first_collimation.speaker: Maya
first_collimation.text_en: At the Collimation Bench, connect the primary to the secondary and the secondary to the focuser. Only then should we take the tube to the Observation Pad.
first_collimation.text_zh: 到准直台先调主镜指向副镜，再把副镜对准调焦器。光轴连成一条线后，我们再去观测。

first_below_horizon.speaker: Maya
first_below_horizon.text_en: The target did not vanish. Earth is simply between our site and that part of the sky, so no amount of telescope movement here can raise it above this horizon.
first_below_horizon.text_zh: 目标并没有消失。只是地球挡在当前地点和那片天空之间，所以在这里无论怎样移动望远镜，都不能让它升到地平线上方。

first_below_horizon.speaker: Maya
first_below_horizon.text_en: Keep the same target and mission. The Observation Site Map will compare real altitude, weather and seeing at other stations, then bring us back to this exact observing step.
first_below_horizon.text_zh: 保留同一个目标和任务。观测地点地图会比较其他站点的真实高度角、天气和视宁度，再把我们带回当前这一步。
